title: import_sieve drops the unused device_isolation rule kind
intention: import_sieve carries only rule kinds something declares.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akienyoga9i at main: git grep finds the device_isolation rule kind only in import_sieve/sieve.py and three tests in its own test_import_sieve.py; no rule set, charter or build_inspector declares it. RULE 1 is build_inspector's encapsulation_holds (124c0312c2d8). The kind split '/'-keyed graph paths on os.sep, so on Windows it found no devices and read green without looking (test_device_isolation_catches_cross_device_import red there). The orchestrator ruled: delete it.
traces_to: Law 3; Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine); Law 8.
how: D1: sieve.py loses the device_isolation docstring paragraph, its elif branch, and its name in the unknown-kind error. D2: test_import_sieve.py loses its three device_isolation tests and their _main entries. D3: outline 1.3.7.1.1 — the callers are checked in the act and nothing checks afterwards. The kind is a branch inside a file, not a path, so `cairn codemother retire` cannot move it aside; the build runs the namers' proof (test_import_sieve.py) before and after the branch leaves, and runs every proof that imports cairn.tools.import_sieve after, recording both in measured_at_build. The proof cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve_stays_green_without_the_unused_kind.py carries only present-tense teeth: the namers' proof runs green, and sole_path still catches. No tooth says the kind stays gone.

out: cairn/tools/base/validation.py (its comment names the device_isolation sieve; another component)
a standing tooth that the kind stays gone (outline 1.3.7.1.1: history kept as code)
the callers' proofs in other components: run at build as a measurement, never a tooth here (RULE 1)
